title: opum-cli-e2e reports lore refusing quest's declared pausedStatus; it does not reproduce on either pair here
description:
REPORTED by opum-cli-e2e 2026-09-17 (their TASK-70) as a reproducible defect: "lore sync/lore check refuse quest's own declared pausedStatus, and lore 0.7.0 is green only because quest renamed to a string lore happens to allow." Their report is well-formed and carries a real exit-6 transcript.

IT DOES NOT REPRODUCE HERE, ON EITHER PAIR. Filed open rather than closed, because a defect someone measured and I could not is a difference between two environments, not an absence.

WHAT I MEASURED, all on throwaway git dirs, binaries resolved by path:
 1. quest 0.6.2 DOES declare the paused status: `task status-flow --json` -> pausedStatus "Blocked". Run from the exact tree opum-cli-e2e named, /Volumes/external/.opum-candidates/0.6.2-full-pair.
 2. quest 0.7.1 declares pausedStatus "Paused".
 3. Lore reads the DECLARED value rather than a literal: src/commands/reconcile-shared.ts:120 calls adapter.pausedStatus?.() and passes it to reconcileStatus (line ~210); src/adapters/quest.ts:397 reads it off `task status-flow`. Present IDENTICALLY in the v0.6.2 and v0.7.0 tags -- 8 refs in quest.ts and 5 in reconcile-shared.ts in both.
 4. quest 0.6.2 + lore 0.7.0, story linked, task paused to "Blocked": `lore sync --json` EXIT 0.
 5. quest 0.6.2 + lore 0.6.2 -- their exact registry-installed pair, both from the path they named -- same fixture: `lore sync --json` EXIT 0.
In 4 and 5 the link was confirmed exit 0 and the task confirmed at status "Blocked" before sync ran.

SO THE PROPOSED FIX SHAPE IS ALREADY IMPLEMENTED. Their acceptance example was "reconcile reads quest task status-flow and admits the declared pausedStatus, so the allowed set comes from the tracker rather than a literal on lore's side". That is what the code does, and it is why 4 passes. On this evidence the current pair's agreement is NOT a coincidence of two independent choices.

THE STRONGEST LEAD, AND IT POINTS AT WHICH BINARY RAN. Their quoted error carries the BACKLOG-flavoured hint: "the task's status must match one of `backlog/config.yml`'s `statuses:` exactly". Backend-conditional hints landed in LCLI-503: the v0.6.2 tag has ZERO refs to statusFlowHints, and 0.7.0/dev supplies QUEST_STATUS_FLOW_HINTS (src/adapters/quest.ts:392). A quest-backed project on a post-LCLI-503 lore should NOT be told to edit backlog/config.yml. So a "byte-identical message" on lore 0.7.0 is the signature of a PRE-LCLI-503 lore, which is the "verify the binary actually running" shape: their 0.7.0 fixture may have resolved to a 0.6.2 lore via PATH or a node_modules/.bin shadow.

STATED AS A LEAD, NOT A VERDICT, because two things stop me concluding it:
 - I could not reproduce even the 0.6.2+0.6.2 failure, which their report measures directly and which the lead does not explain.
 - I could NOT inspect the shipped bundle: @opum-ai/lore/bin/lore.cjs is a launcher shim (0 refs to `backlog/config.yml`, which certainly exists in the product), so the real code is the platform binary and a grep of the .cjs proves nothing either way. I nearly drew a conclusion from that zero before noticing.

ONE CONCRETE DIFFERENCE IN THE PASTED REPRO, worth resolving first: as written it omits the actor context, and `lore link` then exits 6 with quest.actor-context-required (this is LCLI-495's reported case). I had to export LORE_QUEST_ACTOR / LORE_QUEST_ACTOR_KIND to get a link at all. Their harness sets those at process level, so their real fixture differs from the pasted minimal repro in at least that way -- and since reconcile only runs for LINKED tasks, an unlinked fixture would pass rather than fail. So the pasted commands are not the thing that produced their transcript.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS, asked of opum-cli-e2e: from inside the failing fixture, the resolved binary path (`node -e 'console.log(require("fs").realpathSync(process.execPath))'` is not it -- what is wanted is which `lore` ran) and that binary's own `--version`; whether a `backlog/` directory or a `[reconcile]` section existed; and the full `quest task status-flow --json` output from that same fixture. If their lore turns out to be pre-LCLI-503, this closes as already-fixed and their suite rows should pin the version. If it is genuinely 0.7.0, the difference is environmental and worth finding, because then I have a passing case and they have a failing one on the same declared inputs.

NOT GATING ANYTHING: their CI runs the 0.7.0 pair and is green; this repository runs quest 0.7.1 + lore 0.7.0 with nothing parked outside the three-status flow.

SEPARATE AND VALID REGARDLESS OF THE ABOVE -- their own closing point, which they are fixing on their side: reconcile rows that pass for ANY value lore happens to allow do not establish what they are read as establishing. The lore-side equivalent is worth checking: is there a test that a NON-DEFAULT declared pausedStatus is admitted? If every test uses whatever quest currently declares, the suite proves lore tolerates today's string, not that it reads the declaration.
